description: I am a B.Tech Computer Science and Engineering (AI & ML) student interested in AI, web development, data visualization and space science. I am participating in NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026 with the goal of developing EarthPulse, an interactive platform that transforms NASA Earth science visualizations into meaningful audio experiences.
summary:
EarthTune – The Earth Information Jukebox is an interactive web application developed by HackEarth to transform Earth science information into an engaging audio-visual learning experience.

Our project aims to make understanding our planet easier, more interactive and accessible to people of different ages and backgrounds. EarthTune combines web technologies, environmental information, sound generation and educational explanations to help users explore the different systems of Earth.

The application allows users to explore topics such as ocean currents, night-time lights, atmospheric particles and forests. Its Earth Sound experience uses sound patterns to represent Earth-related concepts, helping users understand scientific information through audio. The Earth Guide provides simple educational explanations with voice narration, while the NASA Earth Events section retrieves natural-event information using NASA's EONET API.

Inspired by advances in Earth AI, satellite observations and environmental data science, HackEarth envisions EarthTune as a platform that connects scientific discoveries with interactive technology. Our goal is to encourage environmental awareness, curiosity and learning by presenting complex Earth science concepts in a simple and engaging way.

Through EarthTune, we want people not only to observe our planet but also to experience and understand it through sound, information and exploration.
details:
EarthTune is a web-based educational prototype designed to make Earth science more accessible through interactive exploration and sound. The application is built using HTML, CSS, JavaScript and Node.js with Express.

Its main features include an Earth topic explorer, a sound experience using the Web Audio API, an educational guide with browser-based speech narration, and a natural events section connected to NASA's EONET API.

Users can explore topics such as ocean currents, night-time lights, atmospheric particles and forests. The application converts illustrative data patterns into sound, helping users experience scientific concepts in a different way. The Earth Guide provides educational explanations, while the NASA events section retrieves available natural-event information.

We developed this prototype to encourage curiosity about Earth science and demonstrate how sound, web technologies and accessible explanations can support environmental learning. The project can be expanded with additional NASA datasets, geospatial visualizations and AI-powered analysis.

This describes the working prototype honestly. It does not claim that the current Earth Guide is a generative AI model or that the illustrative sounds are direct recordings from Earth.
